settings.prompt:
Autonomously review this Java source repository for potential security
vulnerabilities using the available read-only tools. Do not ask the user questions or summarize
tool output. Copy exact relative paths from list_files or index results; never invent or prefix a path.
A file listing or index hint is only navigation; inspect original source and seek
counter-evidence before deciding. Trace plausible untrusted input to security-sensitive
operations where possible, and check relevant guards and configuration. Report at most 10
candidates supported by exact source lines, with root cause, preconditions, counter-evidence,
and missing evidence. Do not assume a vulnerability exists. If source review finds no supported
candidate, submit an empty candidate list. Your final action must be submit_findings; natural
language commentary is not a report. Do not use project names, dataset identifiers, or a guessed
known answer as evidence.

counter_evidence: Line 114-115 explicitly disables external entity expansion by default (dataformat-xml#190) when the factory is created internally.
Application can pass its own hardened XMLInputFactory via XmlFactory(XMLInputFactory) / XmlMapper(XMLInputFactory) or via setXMLInputFactory, and can also disable DTD support itself.
The security properties are provider-dependent; some providers disable DTD-related features by default.
candidates.description: XmlFactory constructs the default XMLInputFactory with XMLInputFactory.newInstance() and only sets IS_SUPPORTING_EXTERNAL_ENTITIES to FALSE when no factory is supplied by the caller (XmlFactory.java lines 112-116, comment referencing dataformat-xml#190). It does not set or disable SUPPORT_DTD. A search of the repository returned no occurrence of SUPPORT_DTD. With DTD support left at whatever the underlying Stax provider defaults to, an attacker-controlled XML document that includes a DOCTYPE with internal entity declarations can still cause entity expansion (and, depending on the provider, external general/parameter entities may still be resolved via different property semantics than IS_SUPPORTING_EXTERNAL_ENTITIES). This is a hardening gap in the default parsing configuration used by XmlMapper(), which routes through XmlFactory._createParser -> _xmlInputFactory.createXMLStreamReader(...) (XmlFactory.java lines 534-548, 552-566, 570-588, 591-606). The finding is a candidate, not a confirmed vulnerability: exploitation depends on the concrete Stax implementation present at runtime (Woodstox vs JDK SJSXP) and its default property values, which were not executed or verified here.
missing_evidence: No execution/verification of the runtime Stax provider's default for SUPPORT_DTD.
No test in the repository asserting rejection of DOCTYPE/internal-entity expansion.
No evidence of whether external entity resolution in the chosen provider is fully covered by IS_SUPPORTING_EXTERNAL_ENTITIES alone.
preconditions: Application parses untrusted XML using a default XmlMapper/XmlFactory (no caller-supplied XMLInputFactory).
The runtime Stax provider leaves SUPPORT_DTD enabled by default and/or resolves external entities through semantics not covered by IS_SUPPORTING_EXTERNAL_ENTITIES.
The untrusted XML can contain a DOCTYPE with entity declarations or external references.
candidates.title: Default XmlFactory XMLInputFactory does not disable DTD support (only external entity expansion)
